model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 total revenue (XBRL Revenues / 10-K). The engine's 'ebitda_margin_path' is the AFFO margin on this revenue line, not EBITDA: FY2025 AFFO available to common stockholders $3,885.9M = 67.6% of revenue (H1-2026: $2,079.7M on $3,096.4M = 67.2%). Growth is modelled PER SHARE against a flat share count: year 1 (+9.0%) bridges FY2025 AFFO to the FY2026 guidance midpoint ($4.445/share) on the June-2026 share count, i.e. it carries the accretion from shares already issued; from FY2027 the growth path is per-share AFFO growth NET of the ATM/forward dilution that funds the ~$10B/yr external investment programme. Consolidated revenue will grow faster than this path (H1-2026 +11%); the gap is the dilution.
inputs.share_count_basis: 946.202M common shares at 30 June 2026 (XBRL CommonStockSharesOutstanding; 946.218M on the 10-Q cover at 30 July 2026) + 2.7M Realty Income L.P. common units convertible 1:1 (FY2025 10-K capitalisation note) = 948.9M. AFFO is stated available to common stockholders after NCI, and the OP units share in it, so the divisor includes them. Held FLAT: SBC is charged through sbc_pct_path, and the 22.5M shares under unsettled ATM forward sale agreements (~$1.23B of proceeds at 5 Aug 2026) fund acquisitions not yet made, so their accretion and dilution both sit inside the per-share growth path, not the count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO in the engine by design: AFFO is a post-interest flow capitalised at the cost of equity, so deducting the $30,437.9M net debt again would double-count it (ARG.NZ / PCT.NZ / IPL.NZ / SCG.AX / MAA / BXP treatment). Actual balance sheet at 30 June 2026 recorded in debt_memo.

debt_memo.nci_note: NCI jumped from $685M (Dec-25) to $2,385M (Jun-26) as the U.S. Core Plus Fund and the Apollo JV ($1B for 49%) are consolidated; AFFO available to common already deducts the NCI share, and the unconsolidated JV debt ($3.0B, non-recourse) is outside the consolidated figures.
debt_memo.source: Q2-2026 10-Q (0000726728-26-000048) balance sheet, debt maturity table and net-debt reconciliation; Q2-2026 8-K ex99.1 (0000726728-26-000044) net-debt-inclusive-of-forward-equity reconciliation

inputs.fcf_definition: AFFO available to common stockholders, FY2025 = $3,885.9M (Normalized FFO $3,884.5M +/- debt non-cash items, leasing costs and recurring capex, straight-line rent, above/below-market lease amortisation, credit-loss allowance, SBC add-back; FY2025 10-K reconciliation). Already after interest expense, NCI, and recurring property capex. House (last_fcf) deducts the $30.77M 'amortization of share-based compensation' that Realty Income ADDS BACK into AFFO: 3,885.9 - 30.8 = 3,855.1. Development and acquisition spend is growth capital funded by retained AFFO (~27% after the dividend), debt and equity issuance; it is what the growth path pays for and is not deducted again.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K: cash-flow add-back $30,770k (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation) and the identical 'Amortization of share-based compensation' line added back inside the AFFO reconciliation. Unlike NAREIT FFO, Realty Income's AFFO adds SBC back, so the house basis deducts it once (sbc_pct_path); street basis = reported AFFO. H1-2026 $20.65M (run-rate ~$41M, ~0.65% of revenue).
inputs.buyback_note: H1-2026 repurchases $101.9M (Q1-2026, 10-Q cash-flow statement) under the $2.0B programme expiring Jan-2028 - the first buybacks in the company's history. Against $830.6M of ATM/forward issuance in H1-2026 the company remains a large net issuer; the flat count is a modelling convention (see share_count_basis), not a funded forecast.
inputs.horizon_note: FY0 is FY2025 actual; year 1 is FY2026 (guided, nine months elapsed at the valuation date), years 2-10 are FY2027-FY2035. Discounting the full FY2026 AFFO one year is mildly conservative; the Jan-Sep 2026 monthly dividends have already paid out most of it.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC, because the capitalised flow is post-interest. USD build: 10-year US Treasury 5.24% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-10-01), equity risk premium 5.0%, net-lease REIT beta ~0.85 -> 5.24 + 0.85 x 5.0 = 9.5%. The 5.0% ERP (vs 4.5% used for MAA) reflects O's higher leverage (5.4x net debt/EBITDAre vs 4.5x; screen interest cover 2.35x), ~$31B of debt at a 3.9% average coupon re-pricing toward 4.5-5% over 5.1 years, and a growth model that is wholly dependent on continuous equity and debt issuance (~$10B/yr). Cross-check: at the current price (inputs.price_as_of) the stock yields ~6.1% on the $3.252 dividend and ~8.3% on FY26 guided AFFO, i.e. ~12x AFFO against a 2015-2025 range of roughly 13-21x; a 9.5% CoE with 2.25% terminal growth implies a 14.1x steady-state P/AFFO, the low end of that range. Single rate across scenarios; risk is carried in the paths and the probability weights, not stacked into per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: Realty Income is the lessor under triple-net leases. Ground-lease rent it pays on behalf of clients (~$1.7B undiscounted over 50+ years) is reimbursed by those clients and is inside AFFO.
inputs.nci_treatment: AFFO available to common stockholders is after the NCI share of the consolidated U.S. Core Plus Fund, the Apollo JV and property partnerships ($2,384.5M book at 30-Jun-26); 'AFFO allocable to dilutive noncontrolling interests' ($9.3M FY2025) relates to the 2.7M OP units, which are included in the share count instead. No preferred stock outstanding (Spirit Series A preferred redeemed 2024).
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the Drivers/engine route with net debt held at zero (the GPT.AX/GMG.AX/CHC.AX/MAA pattern). Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md 'REIT / property trust' row: Realty Income is a self-managed US net-lease REIT; GAAP net income is dominated by ~$2.5B/yr of real-estate depreciation and lumpy gains/impairments (P/E 41x is meaningless), OCF less capex is not an owner-FCF series, and the sector is priced on P/AFFO and dividend yield. The engine's components are mapped as: revenue = total consolidated revenue; ebitda_margin_path = street AFFO margin on revenue; sbc_pct_path = SBC/revenue (deducted for the house basis because O adds SBC back into AFFO); D&A, capex, tax and working-capital paths = 0 (recurring capex, leasing costs and the ~$85M/yr of TRS income tax are already inside AFFO). First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). US-GAAP XBRL did not tag total debt (split across NotesPayable / term loans / credit facilities / CommercialPaper / SecuredDebt) or AFFO; both were read from the 10-K/10-Q MD&A tables on EDGAR. The ~1.5% 'cash G&A' and TRS taxes that the investment-management platform brings are inside AFFO. Core-plus Fund and Apollo/KKR/GIC JV fee income is small today (~1% of revenue) and is in the bull path, not the base.

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_basis: House (SBC-deducted) AFFO per diluted share: FY2020 $3.34, FY2022 $3.89, FY2025 $4.25. Reported AFFO per diluted share: FY2017 $3.06, FY2018 $3.19, FY2019 $3.32, FY2020 $3.39, FY2021 $3.59, FY2022 $3.92, FY2023 $4.00, FY2024 $4.19, FY2025 $4.28, H1-2026 $2.22 (+5.2%), FY2026E $4.44-$4.45 (guidance raised Aug-2026). AFFO available to common: FY2019 $1,050.0M, FY2020 $1,172.6M, FY2021 $1,488.8M, FY2022 $2,401.4M, FY2023 $2,774.9M, FY2024 $3,621.4M, FY2025 $3,885.9M. Dividends paid per share: FY2019 $2.7105, FY2020 $2.794, FY2021 $2.833, FY2022 $2.967, FY2023 $3.051, FY2024 $3.1255, FY2025 $3.217; current annualised $3.252 (monthly $0.2710). Revenue, equity and EPS CAGRs are distorted by the VEREIT (Nov-2021, ~$17B) and Spirit (Jan-2024, ~$9B) all-stock mergers: total revenue tripled while AFFO per share compounded ~4%.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Judgment: 10-year house AFFO/share CAGR of the base path (FY2025 $4.25 -> FY2035E $5.79). Sits between the 3-year (+3.0%) and 5-year (+4.9%) per-share AFFO CAGRs; the 5-year figure carries the VEREIT merger accretion and the 2021-22 near-zero cost of capital, neither of which is a run-rate at a 5.2% 10-year Treasury. Equity CAGR is not usable for a REIT (book equity is depreciated cost inflated by stock-funded mergers).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (29.5% 5yr) and revenue CAGR (28.4% 5yr) diverge from EPS (0.3% 5yr) and per-share AFFO (4.9% 5yr) by far more than 30%. Expected: the VEREIT and Spirit mergers were paid in stock, so total revenue and book equity scale with the share count while per-share metrics do not. Growth was therefore selected from the AFFO/share series, not book equity or revenue.
historical_growth.notes: AFFO/share has grown every year since at least FY2017 but the rate has slowed from 4-6% (FY2018-FY2022) to 2-4% (FY2023-FY2026E) as the asset base passed $80B and the cost of capital rose. SBC is 0.5-0.7% of revenue (~$0.03-0.04/share), so house and street per-share values differ by under 1%. The dividend ($3.252 annualised) is 73% of FY26E AFFO; coverage is comfortable and retained AFFO (~$1.1B/yr) funds roughly a tenth of the investment programme.

base.growth_note: Year 1 is the bridge from FY2025 AFFO ($3,885.9M street) to the FY2026 guidance midpoint ($4.445 x 948.9M = $4,218M) on the June-2026 share count; FY2027-FY2035 are per-share AFFO growth rates against a flat count (same-store rent +1.1-1.3% guided, plus ~2-2.5% of spread-investing accretion at a 7.3% initial cash yield against a ~6.5-7% blended cost of capital, fading as the base compounds).
base.ebitda_margin_note: Street AFFO margin on consolidated revenue. FY2025 67.6%, H1-2026 67.2% (the consolidated Fund/Apollo revenue carries an NCI deduction). Drifts to 67.0% as consolidated JV revenue grows and ~$31B of 3.9%-coupon debt rolls toward 4.5-5% (each 100bp on $3B/yr of maturities is ~$30M, ~0.5pt of margin), partly offset by rent recapture above 100% and the capital-light fee stream.
base.narrative: FY2026 lands at the raised guidance ($4.44-4.45 AFFO, ~$10B invested at ~7.3%), then per-share AFFO compounds ~3.5% for three years as the Cloud Capital data-centre JV, GIC industrial build-to-suits and the European book deliver, fading to 2.5% as scale makes each $10B of volume worth less per share. House AFFO/share FY26E $4.40 -> FY30E $5.03 -> FY35E $5.79 (3.1% CAGR), roughly the FY2023-FY2026 cadence. Terminal 2.25% at a 9.5% cost of equity (14.1x AFFO exit); the 17x cap does not bind.

bull.narrative: Rate cuts take the 10-year back toward 4-4.5%: the equity re-rates, the cap-rate/cost-of-capital spread widens to 150bp+, and $10-12B/yr of volume at 7%+ yields becomes 4-5% per-share accretive again (the FY2018-FY2022 regime). The private-capital platform (Core Plus Fund $3.3B AUM, Apollo, KKR, GIC, Cloud Capital $6B) scales fee income to 3-4% of revenue at ~80% margins, lifting the AFFO margin ~120bp. Rent recapture stays above 100% and bad debt stays near 1%. House AFFO/share FY30E ~$5.43, FY35E ~$6.56; terminal 2.75% (15.2x exit, 19x cap not binding).

bear.narrative: Higher-for-longer (10-year above 5%) keeps the equity at a 12x AFFO multiple, so the ~$10B programme shrinks to $4-6B/yr and is barely accretive; $3B/yr of 3.9%-coupon debt rolls at 5-5.5%; and a 2027-28 tenant credit cycle (drugstores, dollar stores, casual dining - top 20 clients are 32% of rent) pushes bad debt to 2-3% of revenue with 300-400bp of margin compression by FY2030. Per-share AFFO growth stalls at 0.5% for two years and recovers only to 1.5-2%; the dividend (73% payout) stays covered so this is a growth problem, not a distribution cut. Terminal 1.5% with a 14x cap (Gordon at 9.5%/1.5% is 12.7x, so Gordon binds).

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance delivered for FY2026, then per-share AFFO compounds ~3-3.5% as the industrial, data-centre and European pipelines plus 1.1-1.3% same-store growth outrun the refinancing drag and the dilution needed to fund ~$10B/yr of investment; the margin drifts 60bp lower as JV revenue consolidates. House AFFO/share compounds 3.1% over ten years, the dividend grows in step, and the exit multiple is 14x AFFO.
scenario_narratives.bull: Falling long rates restore a 150bp+ investment spread and a mid-teens-plus AFFO multiple, volume reaccelerates, and the Apollo/KKR/GIC/Cloud Capital fee platform adds a capital-light earnings stream, so per-share AFFO grows 4-5% for five years and the margin expands to 68.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Rates stay above 5%, the equity stays at ~12x AFFO so external growth is throttled, debt re-prices 100-150bp higher, and a retail tenant credit cycle takes bad debt to 2-3% of revenue; per-share AFFO goes nowhere for three years and the stock is valued as a 1.5% grower at a sub-13x multiple. The A-rated balance sheet, 5.1-year maturities and 73% payout keep this a stagnation case, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the dominant valuation axis - the level of long rates - is outside management's control, O's growth model is wholly dependent on capital-markets access at an accretive multiple, leverage (5.4x) sits above MAA-type peers, and the retail book (73% of rent) carries live tenant-credit risk (Walgreens, dollar stores). Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs rate cuts, spread normalisation and fee-platform scaling to coincide. Not higher on bear: 31 years of unbroken dividend growth, AFFO/share has never fallen in the available history, occupancy 98.8% and rent recapture 103%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Realty Income is valued on the cash it actually distributes - AFFO available to common stockholders, after interest, NCI, recurring capex and (house basis) stock compensation - capitalised at a 9.5% USD cost of equity built off a 5.24% 10-year Treasury, with net debt NOT deducted a second time. Three explicit ten-year per-share AFFO paths bracket the rate regime, the investment spread and tenant credit; the market price is read against where it sits between them. GAAP net income, EPS, P/E, EV/EBITDA and book equity are not used: ~$2.5B/yr of real-estate depreciation, stock-funded mergers and a >100% payout of GAAP earnings make them structurally uninformative for a net-lease REIT.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: every 50bp on the 9.5% discount rate moves base value roughly 7-8%; the 5.24% 10-year Treasury reading is high by post-2009 standards, so the valuation is richer if rates mean-revert and cheaper if they do not
Refinancing: ~$31B of debt at a 3.9% average coupon with 5.1 years average maturity re-prices toward 4.5-5.5%; each 100bp on the full stack is ~$310M (~7%) of AFFO once fully rolled

External-growth dependence: per-share growth above the ~1.2% same-store rate requires issuing equity at a multiple above the acquisition yield; at ~12x AFFO (8.3% yield) against a 7.3% cash yield the spread is thin, and the base path assumes it recovers

Tenant credit: top 20 clients are ~32% of rent; drugstore, dollar-store and casual-dining exposures have produced bankruptcies in 2024-2026 and the bear path carries 300-400bp of margin compression from bad debt

Share count: modelled flat with dilution netted inside the per-share growth path; 22.5M unsettled forward shares and ~$10B/yr of equity-funded volume mean the absolute count will rise materially, so the paths must be read as per-share, not total-company, AFFO
New asset classes: $1.4B into the Cloud Capital hyperscale data-centre JV and European expansion carry underwriting and partner risk outside the retail net-lease core

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close, not after-hours); 52-week range 53.33-67.94, so the price sits at the very bottom of its range
data_sources.financials: SEC EDGAR: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (accession 0000726728-26-000048) for the balance sheet, debt maturity table, net-debt reconciliation, H1-2026 AFFO reconciliation and share count; 8-K ex99.1 Q2-2026 earnings release (0000726728-26-000044) for guidance, investment yields, same-store growth and forward-equity; Form 10-K FY2025 (0000726728-26-000011) for FY2024-FY2025 AFFO, dividends, debt and OP units; Forms 10-K FY2019-FY2023 (0000726728-20-000033 through 0000726728-24-000047) for the AFFO/share and dividend history; SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 726728) for revenue, SBC, shares and D&A as carried in O_Metrics.csv
